rationale: The Latin anchors *compensatio*, *emendatio*, and *reparatio* all point to the legal/remedial sense of making good a wrong or injury, and the attestations are from legal texts (Laws of Æthelberht, Alfred's laws). Among the candidates, *wrong.n.02* ("any harm or injury resulting from a violation of a legal right") best captures this legal-compensatory context; BÓT in Old English fundamentally denotes the compensation or remedy owed for a legal injury, and the gloss token "damage" here stands for the harm that triggers such compensation rather than mere physical deterioration (damage.n.01/03) or a purchase price (price.n.02).
